name: Saudi Arabia
summary: A green field bearing the Shahada, the Islamic declaration of faith, in white Thuluth script above a horizontal sword. Because it carries the Shahada, it is never flown at half-mast and is made with the text reading correctly on both sides.
origin: The flag descends from the banners of the Wahhabi movement and the House of Saud from the 18th century, which were green and bore the Shahada.

Ibn Saud's forces used variations of the green Shahada banner during the unification of the kingdom in the early 20th century; the sword was added in the 1900s–1920s. The design was standardised by law on 15 March 1973.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Islam; green is traditionally associated with the Prophet Muhammad.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Purity; the colour of the inscription and sword.

symbols.name: Shahada
symbols.description: 'There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God', in Arabic Thuluth calligraphy.
symbols.meaning: The Islamic declaration of faith, the first pillar of Islam.

symbols.name: Sword
symbols.description: A horizontal white sword beneath the inscription, pointing toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: Justice and the strength of the House of Saud; commonly linked to Ibn Saud's conquests.

history.label: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

facts: Flags are made double-sided, from two sheets, so the Shahada reads correctly from both sides and the sword points to the hoist on each.
It is never lowered to half-mast, and it is not printed on items such as T-shirts or footballs.
Saudi Arabia marks Flag Day on 11 March, established in 2023.
clues: A green flag with white Arabic calligraphy above a horizontal sword.
It is never flown at half-mast because of the words on it.
It is made double-sided so its inscription reads correctly from both sides.
Its inscription is a declaration of religious faith.
